title: JANUS Engine — AFPM versus micro-EPM startup/commutation screen
closed_cycle_rule: Selective cancellation of a negative PM torque sector is an active motor function. Any apparent positive PM work retained over a cycle must be charged against electrical switching/coil energy; no magnetic energy multiplication is admitted.

micro_EPM_switching_power_screen.interpretation: Milli-joule EPM switching is not automatically excluded by the JANUS auxiliary budget. At 300-600 RPM, an 8-event-per-rev scheme built around roughly 6-10 mJ switching events would consume only about 0.23-0.8 W average in switching itself. However, this says nothing yet about whether such a small EPM can deliver enough torque across the real gap; magnetic force/torque and switching reliability are the decisive missing measurements.

AFPM_torque_screen.interpretation: The current low-tens-of-watts JANUS scale corresponds to sub-Nm shaft torque at 300-600 RPM, making a small coreless AFPM starter-generator a credible baseline pending measured Axle breakaway and running torque.

A_coreless_AFPM.pass_logic: lowest total startup Wh and lowest steady hold watts while retaining regeneration

B_micro_EPM_gated_assist.pass_logic: must reduce total battery Wh versus AFPM-only control by more than all EPM switching/driver losses and complexity penalty

selection_rule: Start with coreless AFPM as baseline hardware/control. Add micro-EPM gated magnetic assist only if bench A/B data proves lower integrated battery energy from S0_OFF through S5_SELF_DRIVE_HOLD without increasing steady-state parasitics or reliability risk.

battery_role.startup: provides controlled torque and all transient auxiliaries
battery_role.transition: absorbs/returns short power deviations while gill/PEMFC states settle
battery_role.proof_rule: external charger off and SOC_end >= SOC_start over stabilized hold

verdict.reason: The AFPM architecture already gives low-cogging startup and regeneration with one mature bidirectional machine; micro-EPM switching is sufficiently low-energy at small scale to deserve a bench comparison, but not enough evidence exists yet to replace AFPM as the baseline.
